title: Decision Making with if, else if and else
learningObjectives: Explain the key idea in decision making with if, else if and else.
Identify the relevant syntax and rules.
Trace each example and predict the result.
Apply the concept in a small program.
Avoid a common mistake related to this topic.

understand.concept: Conditional statements choose which block to execute based on a boolean condition. An if statement runs its block when the condition is true; else if tests additional conditions; else provides a fallback.
understand.whyItMatters: Programs need to respond differently to user input, state, ranges and error conditions.
understand.analogy: Think of this as a control or calculation rule that tells a program how to handle a particular situation consistently.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a starting point; C++ syntax, types and execution rules determine actual behaviour.
understand.explain:
## if and else
The `if` statement evaluates its condition. A following `else` block runs when the condition is false.

## else if chains
Use `else if` to test alternatives in order. Only the first matching branch in the chain executes.

## Block scope and clarity
Braces define blocks and keep statements grouped. Use braces consistently, even for single statements, and avoid deeply nested conditions.

examples.title: Simple condition
examples.explanation: The block runs because the condition is true.

examples.title: Fallback
examples.code: int stock{0};\nif (stock > 0) { std::cout << "Available"; } else { std::cout << "Out of stock"; }
examples.explanation: The else block handles the false condition.

examples.title: Multiple branches
examples.code: int marks{76};\nif (marks >= 90) { std::cout << "A"; } else if (marks >= 70) { std::cout << "B"; } else { std::cout << "C"; }
examples.explanation: The first matching branch is selected.

examples.title: Nested blocks
examples.code: bool member{true}; int points{12};\nif (member) { if (points > 10) { std::cout << "Bonus"; } }
examples.explanation: The inner condition is evaluated only when member is true.

practise.guidedTask: Choose one example from this lesson. Predict its result before running it, change one input or condition, predict again, then explain the difference. Compile and test locally if a C++ compiler is available.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ program that demonstrates decision making with if, else if and else in a meaningful scenario. Include at least two test cases and explain how the code behaves at boundaries or unexpected inputs.
hints: Read the example and identify the exact rule it demonstrates.
Predict output or state changes before compiling.
Change one thing at a time when experimenting.
Use braces and meaningful names to make intent clear.
Test normal, boundary and unexpected cases.
